newsitem.title: ALBANIA: OSCE envoy Vranitzky says Albania mission on track.
newsitem.headline: OSCE envoy Vranitzky says Albania mission on track.

text.p: Franz Vranitzky, international mediator for volatile Albania, said on Wednesday that a multinational security mission was on the right track and there were no near-term plans for troops to disarm Albanians.
Speaking to journalists after landing at Tirana airport, Vranitzky, the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) envoy, said the mission was set up to help Albanians help themselves.

"It's always bad to draw conclusions when a mission starts, but I have the feeling that we are on the right track so far with our mission," Vranitzky said. "Today, our purpose is to enforce it and continue it."

Vranitzky is on a two-day trip to Albania, where he will meet Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and President Sali Berisha. He was also scheduled to travel to the southern town of Vlore and the northern town of Shkoder.

"There are always critics," Vranitzky said when asked why the U.N.-approved force of 6,000 foreign troops would not try to disarm Albanians who seized weapons from army depots during weeks of banditry. Nearly 300 people have been killed.
